DigitalOcean 8 月 1 日調整部分 NVIDIA、AMD GPU 價格，既有鎖價合約不變 » 科技人

# DigitalOcean 8 月 1 日調整部分 NVIDIA、AMD GPU 價格，既有鎖價合約不變 

 黃郁棋 2026 年 7 月 22 日 

DigitalOcean 於 2026 年 7 月 21 日宣布，部分 GPU 服務將在 8 月 1 日調整價格，範圍包含 NVIDIA 與 AMD GPU Droplets 的 on-demand 費率，以及 12 個月 reserved 方案。DigitalOcean 將變動歸因於高階 GPU 容量需求增加，新的計費規則會套用到 8 月 1 日當天仍在執行的工作負載。

DigitalOcean 表示，8 月 1 日後的使用量會依新費率計算，相關費用會反映在 9 月 1 日帳單；若客戶不接受新價格，必須在 8 月 1 日前刪除 GPU Droplets。已簽訂鎖定費率的合約不受這次調整影響，續約時才會套用新的 12 個月 reserved 價格。

### DigitalOcean 8 月 1 日調整 NVIDIA 與 AMD GPU 價格

DigitalOcean 的公告只寫明 select GPUs 會調價，並以頁面表格列出 on-demand 與 12 個月 reserved 的新費率。公告文字沒有逐一列出所有型號的數字，因此不同 GPU、不同區域和不同方案仍應以 DigitalOcean pricing 頁面上的最新表格為準。

這次調整的時間點落在 AI 訓練與 inference 工作負載持續增加的階段。DigitalOcean 將 GPU Droplets、Bare Metal GPUs 和 inference 服務分開列為產品，並非所有 GPU 產品都能從公告直接推定會以相同幅度調整。

### On-demand 工作負載按新費率計帳

對 on-demand GPU Droplets 而言，DigitalOcean 的條款是 8 月 1 日起，當天仍在執行的工作負載即按新價格計費。客戶若在 8 月 1 日之後才停機，已發生的使用量仍會按照更新後的費率計入；若不想承擔調整，停用動作必須在期限前完成。

帳單時間也會拉開決策和付款的間隔。新費率從 8 月 1 日開始累積，費用會在 9 月 1 日帳單呈現，長時間執行的訓練、模型服務和批次 inference 需要把完整週期算入預算，不能只比較建立 Droplet 當天的單價。

### 12 個月 reserved 合約保留原價至期滿

DigitalOcean 表示，若現有 reserved 合約已鎖定費率，8 月 1 日的價格更新不會改變合約單價。合約期滿後選擇續約，才會使用新的 12 個月 reserved 費率；這給固定訓練或長期 inference 工作負載一段確定的成本期間。

這個安排把價格風險集中在續約日。GPU 供應商、區域、數量和工作負載時數若在合約期滿前已變化，團隊仍需比較續約價格、按需用量和轉移到其他雲端的遷移成本；DigitalOcean 沒有在公告中提供客戶個別工作負載的價格保護條款。

### GPU 預算要把續約日與 9 月帳單分開計算

DigitalOcean 目前公開的確定日期包括 8 月 1 日生效與 9 月 1 日反映帳單，已鎖價 reserved 合約則以各自的到期日為界。客戶需要依 GPU 型號和方案重新核對 pricing 頁面的表格，並確認是否有仍在執行的 Droplet 或即將續約的容量。

results.title: Chinese cloud providers hike up prices for cloud and AI services - DCD
highlights:
Several Chinese cloud providers have hiked up the prices for their cloud and AI services.

As reported by The Register, Alibaba Cloud has increased prices for many services by up to 34 percent, while both Tencent and Baidu have followed suit with their own increases.

 

 – Alibaba 

Alibaba Cloud was the first to make the move, sharing a price adjustment notice on March 18 for its "AI computing power and storage products." The increases vary, with GPU-based services increasing between five and 34 percent, and the company's CPFS (Intelligent Computing Edition) services increasing by 30 percent across the board.

These increases are impacting both third-party chips, and Alibaba's home-created AI chips.

The notice puts the increase down to a "surge in global demand and rising supply chain costs," which have meant "the procurement costs of core hardware in the industry have increased significantly."

Just one day later, Baidu Cloud followed suit with its own statement that reads: "Driven by the rapid development of global artificial intelligence applications, the demand for computing power continues to rise.

...

The company has similarly increased prices by between five and 30 percent for AI computing power-related products and services, and 30 percent for parallel file storage.

...

The Chinese cloud providers are not alone in increasing prices - at the start of the year, Amazon Web Services (AWS) increased prices for some of its instances based on the Nvidia H200 GPU. At the time, the company said: "EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML pricing are dynamic and vary based on supply and demand patterns, as described on the product detail page. This price adjustment reflects the supply/demand patterns we expect this quarter."

results.title: Dieses Startup bietet GPU-Leistung auf einer Auktionsplattform an
highlights:
## So wird GPU-Rechenleistung per Auktion angeboten

Das Startup hat den Namen Computable und bietet die Rechenleistung auf der gleichnamigen Webseite an. Die Verantwortlichen schreiben zu dem Projekt auf Hacker News: „Cloud-Computing sieht aktuell aus wie der Energiemarkt vor dem Jahr 2000: Alles wird über bilaterale Verträge geregelt, es gibt keine sichtbaren Preise und nichts davon kann wiederverkauft werden.“

Deshalb haben sie jetzt einen Marktplatz für GPU-Leistung gestartet. Kund:innen können in einer Kalenderansicht aussuchen, für welche Wochen sie die Rechenleistung anmieten wollen, und im Anschluss ein Angebot dafür abgeben. Am Ende gewinnt aber nicht zwangsläufig das Projekt mit dem höchsten Gebot. Laut den Verantwortlichen soll es einen dynamischen Prioritäts-Score geben, der auch kleineren Projekten mit weniger Geld eine Chance auf die Rechenleistung geben soll.

Zum Start der Plattform bietet Computable für den Zeitraum von August 2026 bis Januar 2027 den Zugriff auf H100-Prozessoren von Nvidia. Das Startgebot für die Nvidia-Chips lag bei 2,42 US-Dollar pro GPU‑Stunde. Mittlerweile sind die Preise aber durch erste Gebote schon angestiegen und liegen bei etwa 2,62 Dollar pro Stunde. Für die Nutzung einer einzigen GPU über eine Woche werden so etwas mehr als 300 Dollar fällig.

Ein weiterer Vorteil der Plattform laut den Verantwortlichen: Wer schneller mit der Rechenleistung zum Ziel kommt, kann die restliche Zeit wieder zurückverkaufen. Ungenutzte Wochen können gegen einen von den Betreiber:innen angesetzten Marktpreis wieder zurückgegeben werden. Dadurch machen die Nutzer:innen zwar am Ende immer noch leicht Verlust, aber bleiben nicht auf langfristigen Verträgen und den vollen Kosten sitzen.

results.title: Renting vs Owning GPUs in 2026: When Buying H100s Wins - BuySellRam
highlights:
On-demand H100 SXM instances now list at $3.99 per GPU-hour on specialized GPU clouds like Lambda, with other providers in the same range (RunPod around $2.69, Nebius near $3.15 on a one-year commitment). Marketplace spot capacity has occasionally dipped below $2, though spot is interruptible and both provider- and region-dependent, not a rate to plan a budget around. Hyperscalers cost more for the same silicon: AWS lists its 8×H100 p5.48xlarge at $55.04 per hour, which works out to about $6.88 per GPU-hour. Industry reporting estimated that AWS cut its effective H100 pricing by roughly 44% in June 2025, and the rest of the market followed.

...

## What renting costs in mid-2026

Public price sheets make this the easy half of the equation. A current on-demand menu looks like this per GPU-hour: B200 SXM at $6.69, H100 SXM at $3.99, A100 80GB at $2.79. These vary by region and reservation model — reserved and cluster commitments run lower, while hyperscaler on-demand rates run meaningfully higher for the same silicon.

results.title: AWS cuts costs for H100, H200, and A100 instances by up to 45% - DCD
highlights:
AWS cuts costs for H100, H200, and A100 instances by up to 45% - DCD

# AWS cuts costs for H100, H200, and A100 instances by up to 45%

Cuts commenced this month

June 09, 2025

By
: Georgia Butler 

Amazon Web Services (AWS) has significantly reduced costs for accessing Nvidia H100 and A100 GPUs on its platform.

Revealed by the company on June 5, the price reductions have applied to on-demand purchases since June 1, and to Savings Plans purchases after June 4.

 

 – Getty Images 

The instances impacted are the P4d (A100), P4de (A100), P5 (H100), and P5en (H200).

The on-demand price reduction is 33 percent for A100s across both instance types, 25 percent for the H200 instance type, and 44 percent for the H100 instance.

The 'Savings Plans' cost reduction varies from 25 percent in three years, to 45 percent in three years.

AWS offers two Savings Plans - EC2 Instance and Compute. The former offers the lowest prices in exchange for commitment to use of instances in a Region, while the latter is more flexible regardless of instance type and location. The company has also made the B200 P6 instances available through savings plans.

In a blog post, AWS explained: "Regular price reductions on AWS services have been a standard way for AWS to pass on the economic efficiencies gained from our scale back to our customers."

The company added that high demand for GPU capacity has historically outpaced industry-wide supply, making GPUs more expensive to access.

While AWS puts this reduction down to economies of scale, DCD has previously spoken to Ditlev Bredahl, CEO of host.AI, a company offering a GPU orchestration platform to help GPUaaS providers, who had some concerns about the ongoing economics of GPUs.

“A year ago or so, an H100 was maybe $5-6 per hour. Now, it's around 75 cents, maybe less. Hardware typically depreciates in three to five years, but that's happening in a year now," Bredahl told DCD, though noted that this was more of an issue for neoclouds who have a "one-to-one relationship between the rental property and the customer.”

Bredahl explained: “Let’s say your leasing cost is fixed over three years or even five years. But if your revenue is eroded by 80 percent in just 12 months, then you have a real problem.” In the case of AWS, the reduction of pricing is unlikely to hurt its business in the same way.

AWS made the Nvidia B200 GPUs generally available in May 2025, and the previous generation - the H100s - in July 2023.
